q: Compare last week's performance against this week and identify the likely causes.

checks.what: tool: compares against last week or same weekdays last week

answer:
Short answer
- Revenue and orders fell sharply week-on-week while ad spend also fell; profit improved into small positive territory. Main measured contributors in the catalogue decomposition were a big drop in gross sales and a large rise in P&L return revenue; several ads/campaigns went to zero and Meta activity fell. (See details + suggested next probe.)

Key numbers (same-weekdays comparison: 2026-10-05..2026-10-07 → 2026-10-12..2026-10-14; 10‑14 is partial)
- Net sales: ₹356,317 → ₹133,397; change −₹222,920 (−62.6%). — Measured
- Orders: 188 → 71; change −117 (−62.2%). — Measured
- Ad spend (platform report): ₹215,617 → ₹89,059; change −₹126,558 (−58.7%). — Measured
- Net profit (P&L): −₹19,773 → ₹2,063; change +₹21,836 (+110.4% vs prior loss). — Measured

What the diagnostic decomposition showed (measured, exact accounting)
- Gross sales fell: ₹273,208 → ₹149,743 (effect −₹123,465 on Net sales; ~102% of the Net sales change in the bridge). — Measured
- P&L return revenue jumped: ₹27,175 → ₹118,824 (effect +₹94,631 on the return/cancel line; ~79% of the Net sales change in the bridge). — Measured
- By ad platform, Meta activity dropped (measured): ~₹135,640 → ₹54,144 and accounts for a large share of the movement. — Measured
- Several specific ads dropped to zero (examples flagged): TH-149-SCRATCHLOUNGE, TH-383-SUSPENDER-4XL..., TH-222-WINGBIRD. — Measured

Likely causes (labelled)
- Lower media investment and paused/zeroed ads likely contributed to fewer orders and lower on-site demand. — Hypothesis (supported by measured −58.7% ad spend and ads that went to zero; causal test not run on whole period)
- Spike in returns / return revenue materially changed the P&L decomposition and magnified the net sales movement. — Measured (large jump in P&L return revenue); impact on why revenue behaves this way is a plausible contributor — Hypothesis until tested by day-level return timing.
- Orders fell roughly in line with lower ad spend (both ~−60%); this co-movement is consistent with reduced acquisition but is not proof of causation. — Hypothesis

Data & confidence notes
- All numbers are from the catalogue queries and the diagnostic decomposition. 2026-10-14 is partial; platform spend is from paid_media (platform-reported). The decomposition is exact accounting (reconciles). Some tax lines failed to fetch (not used).

Suggested follow-up (I can run this now)
- Drill down net sales and orders by ad_platform → campaign (top campaigns) and show the return revenue by product/return_date to separate whether returns or ad cuts drove the drop. Which of those would you like me to run?
